newsitem.title: USA: Milton, N.Y. criticized by state comptroller - paper.
newsitem.headline: Milton, N.Y. criticized by state comptroller - paper.

text.p: Milton, N.Y., was criticized by the state Comptroller H. Carl McCall for keeping too much of a surplus and hiring a comptroller who had a conflict of interest, the Albany Times Union said on Sunday.

The 1995 audit and part of the 1996 audit by the state comptroller raised 12 points of other criticisms, including the town's monitoring of its financial activities, documentation of claims, cell phone use, and accountability for gasoline and diesel fuel use.
The town's supervisor told the paper that it had reviewed the criticisims and believed they all had been answered.

Milton's part-time comptroller, who has held the post for 20 years, had been acting as an outside auditing consultant for the town through his work at a consulting firm, which the town paid $10,800 for its services, the audit said, according to the paper.
The town supervisor said the firm stopped working for the town due to the comptroller's criticism, and that its comptroller, who earns $11,200 will stay in his post.

In another matter, the audit said over $700,000 from the general town and highway funds remaining as an unappropriated surplus at the end of 1995 was excessive, and suggested the town adopt more realistic budgets, the Times Union said.
